User & Admin Manual

This document is the official reference guide for all users and administrators of the Everose Marketing Corp. Retail ERP & POS System. It covers day-to-day operations across all modules as well as system configuration, user management, and technical reference.

Developed by Nexarch  ·  Powered by Cyrabell
Part 1 — User Manual

1. Getting Started

This chapter introduces the Everose Marketing Corp. Retail ERP & POS System — what it does, how to access it, and how to navigate its modules. All staff should read this section before using any part of the system.

1.1 System Overview

The Everose ERP & POS System is a fully integrated business platform purpose-built for home appliances and furniture retail. It consolidates point-of-sale, inventory tracking, procurement, supplier management, and financial accounting into a single, browser-based application that requires no installation on individual workstations.

The system is built on a standalone, zero-dependency architecture — the entire application runs from a single HTML file that can be served from any static web host or opened directly from a local file system. There are no separate back-end servers to maintain for the core application logic.

Key Capabilities

  • Point of Sale (POS) — Fast checkout with multiple payment methods, automatic stock deduction, and instant journal posting.
  • Inventory Management — Real-time stock levels across three warehouse locations (Iligan, Ozamis, Dumaguete), reorder alerts, cycle counts, and write-offs.
  • Purchasing & Receiving — Streamlined purchase order creation, supplier management, and goods receipt workflows.
  • Accounting — Double-entry journal engine, Chart of Accounts, Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance, and AR aging.
  • Reports — Sales, inventory valuation, stock health, and supplier spend reports with print and export.
ⓘ Note The system stores all data in the browser's localStorage. Data is device- and browser-specific. See Section 12.4 for important guidance on data persistence and backups.

1.2 Logging In & Navigation

Open the application URL (or the HTML file) in a modern browser (Chrome 110+, Firefox 115+, Edge 110+, or Safari 16+). The system will load directly into the Dashboard.

The top navigation bar provides access to all eight modules:

📊 DashboardBusiness overview & KPIs
🛂 POSPoint of Sale checkout
📦 InventoryProducts & stock levels
📋 PurchasingPurchase Orders
🚚 ReceivingInbound shipments
🏢 SuppliersVendor directory
💰 AccountingLedger & financials
📊 ReportsAnalytics & exports

Click any module name in the top bar to navigate to it. The active module is highlighted. On mobile devices, the navigation bar collapses into a hamburger menu.

✓ Tip Most dialogs and drawers can be closed by pressing Esc. Confirmation prompts can be confirmed with Enter. See the Keyboard Shortcuts table in Section 9 for the full reference.

1.3 Interface Layout

The application follows a consistent layout across all modules:

  • Top Navigation Bar — Module links, brand logo, theme switcher, and density selector.
  • Main Content Area — Tables, forms, cards, and charts specific to the active module.
  • Contextual Right Drawer — Opens when you click a row or record to show details and actions. Close with Esc or the ✕ button.
  • Toast Notifications — Appear in the bottom-right corner for success, warning, and error feedback. They auto-dismiss after 4 seconds.

Theme Toggle

The top navigation bar contains a theme toggle with three options:

  • Light — White background, dark text (default).
  • Dark — Dark background, light text. Recommended for low-light environments.
  • System — Follows your operating system's color scheme preference automatically.

Density Setting

The interface supports two density modes, selectable from the tweaks panel in the top bar:

  • Compact — Reduced row height and padding; shows more data on screen. Best for power users and data-entry roles.
  • Comfy — Default spacing with generous padding; easier to read and tap on touchscreens.

2. Point of Sale (POS)

The POS module is the primary interface for front-of-house staff. It handles all customer transactions — from adding items to the cart through final payment — while automatically updating inventory and accounting records in real time.

2.1 Opening the POS

  1. Click POS in the top navigation bar. The POS screen loads, showing the product search panel on the left and the order cart on the right.
  2. Verify that the correct warehouse location is selected in the location selector (top of the POS panel). This determines which warehouse's stock levels are checked at checkout.
  3. Confirm the transaction date shown is correct. The system defaults to today's date.
  4. The POS is now ready. You may begin searching for products.
⚠ Warning Always select the correct warehouse before starting a transaction. If you sell from the wrong warehouse location, stock levels at that location will be incorrectly decremented. Corrections require a manual stock adjustment (Section 3.4).

2.2 Searching for Products

The product search bar supports two search modes:

  • SKU Search — Type the exact SKU code (e.g., AP-001) to immediately locate a specific product. SKU codes are printed on product tags and purchase orders.
  • Name Search (Fuzzy) — Type any part of the product name. The system uses a fuzzy Levenshtein-distance algorithm that tolerates minor typos and partial matches. For example, typing refrig will return all refrigerator products. Typing LG 55 will return LG 55-inch television models.

Results appear as a scrollable card list below the search bar, showing the product name, SKU, current stock at the selected warehouse, and selling price. Products with Out of Stock status are shown but cannot be added to the cart unless the supervisor override is enabled.

✓ Tip Press F2 from anywhere in the POS screen to instantly focus the search bar. This is faster than clicking with the mouse.

2.3 Adding Items to the Cart

  1. Search for the product (Section 2.2).
  2. Click the product card or press Enter when a product is highlighted to add one unit to the cart.
  3. To add multiple units immediately, type the desired quantity in the quantity field next to the product before clicking Add, or adjust the quantity in the cart after adding.
  4. In the cart panel, use the + and − buttons to adjust line quantities. You can also click the quantity number and type a new value directly.
  5. To remove a line item from the cart, click the trash icon on that line, or set the quantity to zero.

The cart automatically recalculates subtotals as items are added or quantities are changed. The order summary at the bottom of the cart shows: Subtotal, Discount, Tax (if applicable), and Total.

2.4 Applying Discounts

Discounts can be applied at two levels:

Line-Item Discount

  1. Click the discount icon (%) on any cart line item.
  2. Enter the discount as a percentage (e.g., 10 for 10%) or as a fixed peso amount (e.g., ₱500).
  3. The discounted price and savings amount update immediately on the line.

Order-Level Discount

  1. Click the Apply Discount button in the cart summary area.
  2. Enter a percentage or fixed amount. This discount is applied to the entire order subtotal after individual line discounts.
  3. Click Confirm or press Enter.
ⓘ Note Discounts are recorded in the transaction journal as a debit to the Sales Discount account and are visible on the printed receipt. Managers may have authority limits on discount percentages — check with your supervisor.

2.5 Payment Methods

The system supports six payment methods. Select one (or split across multiple) in the payment dialog:

MethodDescriptionNotes
CashPhysical currency paymentEnter tendered amount; system calculates change automatically.
Credit CardVisa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.Enter card type and last 4 digits for reference. No terminal integration — manual entry only.
GCashGCash mobile walletEnter GCash reference number from the customer's app or SMS receipt.
MayaMaya (PayMaya) mobile walletEnter Maya reference number. Confirm customer app screenshot if required.
CheckPersonal or company checkEnter check number, bank name, and check date. Manager approval required for post-dated checks.
Terms / ARCharge to customer account (30/60/90-day terms)Customer must have an active AR account. Creates an AR entry in Accounting. Requires manager approval.

Split Payment

To split a payment across multiple methods (e.g., partial GCash + cash balance):

  1. In the payment dialog, click Add Payment Method.
  2. Select the first method and enter the partial amount.
  3. Click Add Another and select the second method for the remaining balance.
  4. The dialog will show the total tendered versus the order total. Confirm when balanced.

2.6 Completing a Sale

  1. Verify the cart contents and totals are correct.
  2. Click Charge or press F4 to open the payment dialog.
  3. Select the payment method(s) and enter amounts.
  4. Click Complete Sale or press Enter.
  5. The system performs the following actions automatically and simultaneously:
    • Deducts sold quantities from stock at the selected warehouse.
    • Posts a double-entry journal: Debit Cash/AR · Credit Sales Revenue; Debit COGS · Credit Inventory.
    • Creates a transaction record with a unique receipt number.
    • Displays the receipt preview dialog.
✓ Tip If a product goes out of stock mid-transaction (e.g., another terminal sells the last unit), the system will show a warning before allowing completion. You can choose to proceed with the available quantity or remove the item.

2.7 Printing a Receipt

After a sale is completed, the receipt preview dialog appears automatically. From this dialog:

  • Click Print Receipt to send to the default system printer (80mm thermal or standard A4).
  • Click Save as PDF to download a PDF copy.
  • Click Email Receipt to send a copy to a customer email address (if email is configured).
  • Click New Sale to clear the cart and start the next transaction without printing.

The receipt includes: store name and address, receipt number, date and time, cashier name, line items with quantities and prices, discounts, payment method breakdown, and change/balance.

ⓘ Note To reprint a past receipt, navigate to Reports → Sales Report, find the transaction by date or receipt number, and click Print on the transaction row.

3. Inventory Management

The Inventory module provides a real-time view of all products and their stock levels across all warehouse locations. It is the central hub for product information, stock monitoring, and inventory adjustments.

3.1 Product List Overview

The main Inventory screen displays a paginated table of all products. Each row shows:

  • SKU — Unique product identifier (e.g., AP-001).
  • Product Name — Full descriptive name including brand and model.
  • Category — Product category (e.g., Refrigerators, Washing Machines, Sofas).
  • Total Stock — Combined stock across all warehouses.
  • Status Badge — Color-coded stock health indicator (see Section 3.5).
  • Cost — Weighted average cost per unit.
  • Price — Current selling price.
  • Reorder Point — Minimum stock threshold that triggers a reorder alert.

Status badges displayed in the product list:

OK Watch Low Out of Stock

3.2 Searching & Filtering

Use the toolbar above the product list to locate products quickly:

  • Search Bar — Fuzzy search across SKU, product name, and category. Tolerates minor typos. Results update in real time as you type.
  • Category Filter — Dropdown to filter by product category. Select "All Categories" to clear the filter.
  • Warehouse Filter — Show stock levels for a specific warehouse location (Iligan, Ozamis, or Dumaguete) instead of the combined total.
  • Status Filter — Filter to show only products with a specific stock status (e.g., show only Low and Out of Stock items).
✓ Tip Press Ctrl+F to instantly focus the inventory search bar without clicking.

3.3 Product Detail Drawer

Click any product row to open the Product Detail Drawer on the right side of the screen. The drawer contains:

  • Stock Per Location — A breakdown of on-hand quantity at each warehouse: WH-ILIGAN, WH-OZAMIS, WH-DUMAGUETE.
  • In-Transit Stock — Units on open Purchase Orders not yet received.
  • Cost & Pricing — Weighted average cost, last purchase cost, and current selling price.
  • Reorder Settings — Reorder point and suggested reorder quantity.
  • Transaction History — Recent stock movements (sales, receipts, adjustments) for this product.

From the drawer, you can:

  • Click Edit Product to update the product's name, category, price, or reorder settings (Admin/Manager only).
  • Click Adjust Stock to create a stock adjustment (Section 3.4).
  • Click Create PO to immediately start a Purchase Order pre-filled with this product (Section 4.1).

3.4 Stock Adjustments

Use stock adjustments to correct inventory records when the physical count does not match the system count, or to record damaged or lost goods. There are three adjustment types:

TypeWhen to UseAccounting Effect
Cycle Count Physical count differs from system count; correcting a discrepancy without a specific reason. Debits or credits the Inventory Adjustment account to reflect the variance.
Write-Off Stock is damaged, stolen, or expired and must be removed from inventory. Debits Inventory Loss/Write-Off expense; Credits Inventory asset.
Transfer Moving stock between warehouse locations (e.g., WH-ILIGAN to WH-OZAMIS). No P&L impact; updates stock quantities at source and destination warehouses.

Performing a Stock Adjustment

  1. Open the Product Detail Drawer for the product to adjust (click the product row).
  2. Click Adjust Stock.
  3. Select the adjustment type (Cycle Count, Write-Off, or Transfer).
  4. Select the warehouse location. For Transfers, select both source and destination.
  5. Enter the quantity to adjust. For Cycle Count, enter the new on-hand quantity (not the difference). For Write-Off and Transfer, enter the number of units to remove/move.
  6. Enter a reason/note for the adjustment (required for audit purposes).
  7. Click Confirm Adjustment. The system updates stock levels and posts the appropriate journal entry.
⚠ Warning Stock adjustments are permanent and create accounting entries. Double-check quantities before confirming. If an error is made, a correcting adjustment must be entered — there is no undo.

3.5 Stock Status Thresholds

Each product's stock status is determined by comparing the current on-hand quantity against the product's Reorder Point:

StatusConditionRecommended Action
OK On-hand > Reorder Point × 1.5 No action needed. Stock is healthy.
Watch On-hand between Reorder Point × 1.0 and × 1.5 Monitor closely. Consider placing a PO soon.
Low On-hand > 0 but ≤ Reorder Point Create a Purchase Order immediately (see Section 4.1).
Out of Stock On-hand = 0 Urgent: reorder and notify sales team. POS will block sales by default.

3.6 Command Center — Bulk Reorder View

The Command Center is a dedicated view accessible from the Inventory module's toolbar (click Command Center button). It shows all products currently at Low or Out of Stock status in a prioritized list, grouped by supplier.

From the Command Center you can:

  • Select multiple products using checkboxes and click Bulk Create PO to generate Purchase Orders for all selected items at once.
  • Override suggested reorder quantities before creating POs.
  • Filter by warehouse to see location-specific shortages.
  • Export the list as a CSV for emailing to suppliers.
✓ Tip Run the Command Center view every morning as part of the opening routine to catch any overnight stock depletions from previous-day sales.

4. Purchasing & Purchase Orders

The Purchasing module manages the entire purchase order lifecycle — from creation through approval, delivery, and closure. All purchase orders integrate with the Receiving module and automatically update Inventory and Accounting upon receipt.

4.1 Creating a Purchase Order

  1. Navigate to Purchasing in the top navigation bar.
  2. Click the New PO button in the top-right of the Purchase Orders list.
  3. Select the Supplier from the dropdown. If the supplier is not listed, add them first in the Suppliers module (Section 6).
  4. Select the Destination Warehouse — the location where goods will be received.
  5. Set the Expected Delivery Date.
  6. Add line items:
    • Click Add Product and search for the product by SKU or name.
    • Enter the quantity and confirm the unit cost (pre-filled from last purchase price).
    • Repeat for each product.
  7. Review the PO total and add any notes for the supplier in the Remarks field.
  8. Click Save as Draft to save without sending, or Submit PO to change status to Open and make it available for receiving.

4.2 Suggested Reorders

When creating a new PO, the system can automatically suggest products and quantities based on current stock levels:

  1. In the New PO form, after selecting a supplier, click Load Suggestions.
  2. The system fills the PO with all products from that supplier that are currently at Low or Out of Stock status, with quantities set to reach double the reorder point.
  3. Review and adjust the suggested quantities as needed before saving.
✓ Tip The Command Center (Section 3.6) also allows bulk PO creation across multiple suppliers. Use it when you need to reorder from several vendors at once.

4.3 PO Statuses

StatusDescriptionNext Action
Draft PO has been created but not yet submitted. Stock is not affected. Can be edited freely. Review, edit, then Submit to make Open.
Open PO has been submitted and is awaiting delivery. No goods received yet. Receive goods in the Receiving module.
Partial Some (but not all) line items have been received. The PO remains open for remaining quantities. Receive remaining goods. Contact supplier for outstanding items.
Closed All line items have been fully received and the PO is complete. No further receipts can be posted. File for records. PO is read-only.

4.4 Editing and Approving POs

POs in Draft status can be freely edited by the Purchasing Officer. Once submitted (status becomes Open), editing requires Manager approval.

To edit an Open PO:

  1. Open the PO from the Purchasing list.
  2. Click Request Edit. This sends an approval request notification.
  3. A Manager must approve the edit request from their notifications panel.
  4. Once approved, the PO temporarily returns to a Draft-like editable state.
  5. Make changes, then re-submit. A new approval may be required depending on the value change.
ⓘ Note POs in Partial or Closed status cannot be edited. If a correction is needed on a closed PO, a new adjustment PO or stock adjustment must be created.

4.5 Printing a Purchase Order

  1. Open the PO from the Purchasing list.
  2. Click the Print PO button (or press Ctrl+P).
  3. A print-optimized PO document opens in a new tab, showing the company header, supplier details, line items, quantities, unit costs, totals, and authorization signature lines.
  4. Use your browser's print dialog to print or save as PDF.

The printed PO can be emailed or faxed to the supplier as the official order document.

5. Receiving

The Receiving module manages the receipt of goods against Purchase Orders. When goods arrive from a supplier, the Stock Clerk uses this module to record the receipt, which triggers automatic inventory updates and accounting entries.

5.1 Viewing Inbound Shipments

Navigate to Receiving in the top navigation bar. The screen shows a list of all open POs that are awaiting receipt, grouped by expected delivery date. Each row shows:

  • PO number and creation date
  • Supplier name
  • Destination warehouse
  • Expected delivery date
  • Total value of outstanding items
  • PO status (Open or Partial)

Click any row to open the Receiving Form for that PO.

5.2 Receiving Goods Against a PO

  1. From the Receiving list, click the PO for which goods have arrived.
  2. The Receiving Form shows all line items on the PO, with columns for: Product, SKU, Ordered Qty, Previously Received, Outstanding Qty, and Received Now.
  3. For each product that arrived, enter the quantity received in the Received Now column. Do not enter more than the outstanding quantity.
  4. Enter the Delivery Reference (supplier's delivery note number, waybill number, or DR number). This is required for audit purposes.
  5. Select the correct warehouse location where goods will be stocked.
  6. Review unit costs — the system pre-fills the PO cost. If the actual invoice price differs, update it here. This affects the weighted average cost calculation.
  7. Click Confirm Receipt.

5.3 Partial vs. Full Receipt

Full Receipt — You receive 100% of all outstanding quantities on the PO. The PO status changes to Closed.

Partial Receipt — You receive some but not all items. The PO status changes to Partial. The PO remains in the Receiving queue for future receipts when the remaining goods arrive.

✓ Tip If a supplier will never deliver the remaining items on a Partial PO (e.g., discontinued product, cancelled line), a Manager can manually close the PO from the Purchasing module. This will mark the undelivered lines as cancelled.

5.4 Automatic Stock Update

Upon confirming a receipt, the system automatically:

  • Adds the received quantities to on-hand stock at the destination warehouse.
  • Recalculates the weighted average cost for each received product.
  • Posts a double-entry journal: Debit Inventory Asset · Credit Accounts Payable (for the received value at PO cost).
  • Updates the PO status to Partial or Closed.
  • Creates a Goods Receipt record with the delivery reference number for auditing.
⚠ Warning Ensure physical goods are counted and verified before confirming receipt in the system. Confirmed receipts create accounting entries and cannot be reversed without a correcting stock adjustment and journal entry.

6. Suppliers

The Suppliers module maintains the directory of all vendors from whom Everose Marketing Corp. purchases products. Accurate supplier records are essential for purchase order management and accounts payable tracking.

6.1 Supplier List

Navigate to Suppliers in the top navigation bar. The list shows all registered suppliers with their contact information, number of open POs, and outstanding payable balance. Use the search bar to find a supplier by name, contact person, or phone number.

Click Add Supplier to register a new vendor (requires Admin or Purchasing Officer role). Fill in:

  • Company/Business name
  • Contact person name and title
  • Phone and email address
  • Business address
  • Payment terms (e.g., Net 30, Net 60, COD)
  • Tax Identification Number (TIN) — required for BIR-compliant purchasing records

6.2 Supplier Details

Click any supplier row to open the Supplier Detail view. This shows the full supplier profile, a list of associated products (products that have been ordered from this supplier), and the current accounts payable balance.

From the Supplier Detail view, you can:

  • Edit supplier information (Admin only)
  • Create PO — Start a new Purchase Order with this supplier pre-selected
  • View Purchase History — See all historical POs and receipts
  • Record Payment — Post an AP payment (Accountant role required)

6.3 Purchase History

The Purchase History tab within the Supplier Detail view shows a chronological list of all Purchase Orders for this supplier. Each entry shows: PO number, date, total value, status, and linked goods receipts. Click any PO to navigate directly to that Purchase Order's details.

A summary panel at the top shows: total purchases year-to-date, average order value, number of orders this year, and current outstanding AP balance.

7. Accounting

The Accounting module implements a full double-entry bookkeeping engine. All transactions across POS, Purchasing, and Receiving automatically create journal entries. Accountants can review, manually adjust, and generate financial statements from this module.

7.1 Chart of Accounts Overview

The Chart of Accounts (CoA) is the structured list of all financial accounts used by the system. It follows standard Philippine accounting practice and is organized into five top-level categories:

Code RangeCategoryNormal BalanceExamples
1000–1999AssetsDebitCash, Accounts Receivable, Inventory, Fixed Assets
2000–2999LiabilitiesCreditAccounts Payable, Accrued Expenses, Loans Payable
3000–3999EquityCreditOwner's Capital, Retained Earnings
4000–4999RevenueCreditSales Revenue, Other Income
5000–5999ExpensesDebitCOGS, Salaries, Rent, Utilities, Depreciation

Key accounts used by the system's automatic journal engine:

CodeAccount NameDescription
1010Cash — Petty CashCash on hand at POS counters
1020Cash — BankBank account balances
1100Accounts ReceivableAmounts owed by credit customers (Terms sales)
1200InventoryValue of goods on hand (asset)
2100Accounts PayableAmounts owed to suppliers
4010Sales RevenueRevenue from product sales
4020Sales DiscountsContra-revenue for granted discounts
5010Cost of Goods SoldInventory cost recognized at point of sale
5900Inventory Write-OffLoss from damaged or stolen goods

7.2 Journal Entries

Navigate to Accounting → Journal Entries to view all posted entries. The list is sorted newest-first and shows: entry date, reference number, description, debit total, credit total, and posting status.

All auto-posted entries (from POS sales, receiving, adjustments) are labeled with their source module (e.g., [POS], [RECV], [ADJ]). These cannot be deleted — they can only be reversed by creating a correcting entry.

Manual Journal Entry

To post a manual journal entry (Accountant role required):

  1. Click New Entry.
  2. Enter the entry date and a description.
  3. Add debit lines: select account and enter amount.
  4. Add credit lines: select account and enter amount.
  5. Ensure debits equal credits (the system will alert if they are unbalanced).
  6. Click Post Entry. The entry is immediately reflected in all financial reports.

7.3 Profit & Loss

Navigate to Accounting → Profit & Loss. The P&L statement shows:

  • Revenue — Total sales revenue for the period, broken down by product category if enabled.
  • Less: Cost of Goods Sold — Total COGS recognized during the period.
  • Gross Profit — Revenue minus COGS.
  • Operating Expenses — All expense accounts (rent, salaries, utilities, etc.).
  • Net Profit / (Loss) — Gross Profit minus Operating Expenses.

Use the date range picker at the top to set the reporting period (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or custom range). Click Print Statement to print or export as PDF.

7.4 Balance Sheet

Navigate to Accounting → Balance Sheet. The Balance Sheet shows the company's financial position at a specific date (point-in-time). It presents:

  • Assets — Current Assets (Cash, AR, Inventory) and Non-Current Assets (Fixed Assets, net of depreciation).
  • Liabilities — Current Liabilities (AP, Accrued Expenses) and Long-Term Liabilities.
  • Equity — Owner's Capital plus Retained Earnings (including current period net income).

The Balance Sheet will always balance: Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity. If it does not balance, there is a data integrity issue — contact the system administrator immediately.

7.5 Trial Balance

Navigate to Accounting → Trial Balance. The Trial Balance lists every account in the Chart of Accounts with its cumulative debit and credit totals and net balance for the selected period. It is used to verify that all journal entries are balanced before preparing the P&L and Balance Sheet.

The footer of the Trial Balance shows the grand totals for all Debit and Credit columns — these must be equal. Use the Filter Zero Balances toggle to hide accounts with no activity in the period.

7.6 Accounts Receivable

Navigate to Accounting → Accounts Receivable. This view shows all outstanding customer balances from sales made on Terms. The AR Aging report categorizes outstanding balances by age:

Aging BucketDescription
CurrentNot yet due (within payment terms)
1–30 DaysOverdue by 1 to 30 days
31–60 DaysOverdue by 31 to 60 days
61–90 DaysOverdue by 61 to 90 days — Flag for collection follow-up
90+ DaysSeriously overdue — Escalate for management review

To record a customer payment against an AR balance, click the customer row and click Record Payment. Enter the payment amount, date, and reference number. The system debits Cash and credits AR.

7.7 Printing Statements

All financial statements (P&L, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance, AR Aging) include a Print / Export button. The printed format includes the company name, report title, date range, and page numbers. Use Ctrl+P as a quick print shortcut from any financial report view.

ⓘ Note Financial statements are generated in real time from the journal entries database. Ensure all entries for the period have been posted before printing official financial statements for management review or tax filing.

8. Reports

The Reports module provides analytical views and exportable data summaries across all areas of the business. All reports support date range filtering and can be printed or exported.

8.1 Sales Reports

Navigate to Reports → Sales. Available views include:

  • Daily Sales Summary — Total revenue, number of transactions, average transaction value, and payment method breakdown for each day.
  • Sales by Product — Units sold, revenue, and gross margin per product for the selected period. Sort by any column.
  • Sales by Category — Category-level rollup of sales performance.
  • Sales by Cashier — Per-staff breakdown of transactions and revenue. Useful for performance review.
  • Transaction Log — Complete list of all transactions with receipt number, date/time, items, total, payment method, and cashier. Click any row to view or reprint the receipt.

8.2 Inventory Valuation

Navigate to Reports → Inventory Valuation. This report shows the current monetary value of all inventory on hand, calculated as: On-Hand Qty × Weighted Average Cost. It can be viewed as:

  • Total Valuation — One aggregate number for all inventory.
  • By Product — Per-SKU breakdown of quantity and value.
  • By Warehouse — Valuation broken down by WH-ILIGAN, WH-OZAMIS, and WH-DUMAGUETE.
  • By Category — Rollup by product category.

8.3 Stock Health Report

Navigate to Reports → Stock Health. This report shows the distribution of products across the four stock status tiers (OK, Watch, Low, Out of Stock) with totals and percentages. A bar chart gives a visual overview. The detail table lists every product with its current status, on-hand quantity, reorder point, and days of supply estimate (based on average daily sales velocity over the past 30 days).

8.4 Supplier Spend Report

Navigate to Reports → Supplier Spend. This report shows purchasing spend by supplier for the selected period, including: total PO value, total received value, number of orders, on-time delivery rate, and average lead time. Use this report to evaluate supplier performance and negotiate terms.

8.5 Export & Print Pack

Every report in the system supports the following export options:

  • Print — Opens a print-optimized view in a new browser tab. Press Ctrl+P to print or save as PDF.
  • Export CSV — Downloads the report data as a comma-separated values file, compatible with Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.
  • Export PDF — Generates a formatted PDF document (uses browser print-to-PDF under the hood).
✓ Tip For a complete end-of-month reporting pack, run the following in order: (1) Inventory Valuation, (2) Sales by Product, (3) Profit & Loss, (4) Balance Sheet, (5) AR Aging. Export each as PDF and compile into a single document.

Part 2 — Admin Manual

9. System Configuration

This section covers the initial setup and ongoing configuration of the system. Configuration tasks require the Administrator role and should only be performed by qualified personnel.

9.1 Data Structure Overview

The system's data is organized into the following primary entities and their relationships:

  • Products — Master product catalog. Each product has stock records per warehouse.
  • Warehouses — Physical locations. Each warehouse holds independent stock quantities per product.
  • Suppliers — Vendor directory. Suppliers are linked to products (for reorder suggestions) and POs.
  • Purchase Orders — Procurement documents. Linked to suppliers, products, and warehouse destinations.
  • Transactions — POS sale records. Each transaction creates journal entries and decrements inventory.
  • Journal Entries — Double-entry accounting records. Auto-generated by system events and manually created by accountants.
  • Accounts — The Chart of Accounts. Parent-child hierarchy with code-based organization.

All data is persisted in the browser's localStorage as serialized JSON. The application loads seed data on first launch; subsequent visits use stored data.

9.2 Adding Products

Navigate to Inventory and click Add Product.

SKU Format

SKUs follow the format CC-NNN where CC is a two-letter category code and NNN is a three-digit sequential number. Examples:

CategoryCodeExample SKU
Appliances (general)APAP-001, AP-002
RefrigeratorsRFRF-001, RF-002
Washing MachinesWMWM-001
Air ConditionersACAC-001
TelevisionTVTV-001
FurnitureFNFN-001
Bedroom FurnitureBDBD-001
Living RoomLRLR-001

Required Product Fields

  • SKU — Unique identifier. Must not duplicate existing SKUs.
  • Product Name — Full descriptive name (include brand and model number).
  • Category — Select from existing categories or create a new one.
  • Unit — Unit of measure (e.g., "pcs", "set", "unit").
  • Selling Price — Default retail price (can be overridden at POS with appropriate permission).
  • Cost — Initial cost price. Updated automatically by weighted average when goods are received.
  • Reorder Point — Minimum stock level that triggers Low/Watch alerts.
  • Reorder Qty — Suggested quantity for purchase orders.
  • Default Supplier — Primary supplier (for reorder suggestions).
  • Initial Stock per Warehouse — Opening stock quantity at each warehouse on creation.

9.3 Adding Warehouses

The system comes pre-configured with three warehouse locations. These should not be renamed without updating all dependent data. If additional warehouses are needed, add them via Admin → Warehouses → Add Warehouse.

CodeNameLocation
WH-ILIGANIligan BranchIligan City, Lanao del Norte
WH-OZAMISOzamis BranchOzamis City, Misamis Occidental
WH-DUMAGUETEDumaguete BranchDumaguete City, Negros Oriental

Each warehouse has a: code, name, address, contact person, and active/inactive status. Inactive warehouses are hidden from POS location selectors and receiving forms.

9.4 Adding Suppliers

Navigate to Suppliers → Add Supplier. All fields in Section 6.1 are relevant here. Additionally, admins can:

  • Set the default payment terms (Net 15, Net 30, Net 60, COD, etc.) which will pre-fill on new POs for this supplier.
  • Assign products to a supplier (for reorder suggestion linking).
  • Set a credit limit for AP tracking.

9.5 Chart of Accounts Setup

The Chart of Accounts is pre-populated with standard accounts on first launch. To add or modify accounts, navigate to Accounting → Chart of Accounts → Manage Accounts.

✖ Caution Do not delete or reassign the system-reserved accounts (codes 1010, 1100, 1200, 2100, 4010, 4020, 5010). These are used by the automatic journal engine. Deleting them will cause errors on POS transactions, receiving, and stock adjustments. Contact Nexarch support before making structural changes to the CoA.

The system uses a role-based access control (RBAC) model. Each user account is assigned exactly one role, which determines which modules and actions they can access.

11. Technical Architecture

This section is intended for IT staff and system administrators who need to understand how the application is built, deployed, and maintained.

11.1 Technology Stack

ComponentTechnologyVersionNotes
UI FrameworkReact18.3.1Loaded via CDN (unpkg). No npm install required.
JavaScript CompilerBabel Standalone7.xTranspiles JSX in the browser at load time. No build step needed.
StylingVanilla CSS—Embedded in <style> tags. No CSS framework dependency.
FontsIBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono—Loaded from Google Fonts CDN.
Data PersistencelocalStorage (browser)—JSON serialization. ~5–10MB limit typical per origin.
Search EngineCustom Levenshtein fuzzy search—Pure JavaScript, no external library. See Section 11.4.
Print / PDFBrowser native print API—CSS @media print with dedicated print stylesheets per document type.
DeploymentSingle HTML file—No server required. Can serve from any static host or file:// protocol.
ⓘ Note Because Babel transpiles JSX in the browser, initial page load on first visit (or after cache clear) may take 2–4 seconds on older hardware. Subsequent loads use the browser's script cache and are significantly faster. For best performance, use Chrome or Edge on a modern PC or laptop.

11.2 File Structure

The application is composed of 15 module files, all embedded or referenced within the single HTML entry point:

#FilePurpose
1app.jsxRoot component. Manages global state, routing between modules, and theme/density state.
2data.jsSeed data and localStorage read/write utilities.
3components.jsxShared UI components (buttons, badges, modals, toasts, form fields).
4theme.cssCSS custom properties and global styles.
5dashboard.jsxDashboard module — KPI cards, charts, quick stats.
6pos.jsxPOS module — product search, cart, payment dialog, receipt.
7inventory.jsxInventory module — product list, filters, detail drawer.
8inventory-command.jsxInventory Command Center — bulk reorder view.
9adjust.jsxStock adjustment forms (Cycle Count, Write-Off, Transfer).
10po.jsxPurchasing module — PO list, create/edit PO form.
11receiving.jsxReceiving module — inbound list, receiving form.
12drawer.jsxReusable right-panel drawer component.
13accounting.jsxAccounting module — journal entries, CoA, financial statements.
14reports.jsxReports module — all report views and export handlers.
15printdocs.jsxPrint-optimized document templates for receipts, POs, and financial statements.

Additionally, accounts-data.js contains the default Chart of Accounts seed data, and tweaks-panel.jsx provides the theme/density settings panel.

11.3 Print / PDF System

The print system uses the browser's native window.print() API with CSS @media print rules to generate clean, formatted documents. Each document type (receipt, PO, financial statement) has a dedicated print template in printdocs.jsx.

When a user triggers a print action:

  1. The system renders the print template into a hidden <div> or a new browser tab.
  2. CSS print rules hide all navigation, sidebars, and interactive elements.
  3. The document is formatted for standard A4 or 80mm thermal paper based on the document type.
  4. window.print() is called, opening the system print dialog.
  5. The user selects their printer or "Save as PDF" and confirms.

11.4 Search Engine — Fuzzy / Levenshtein

The application implements a custom fuzzy search engine based on the Levenshtein edit-distance algorithm. This is used in POS product search and inventory filters.

The algorithm works as follows:

  1. The search query is normalized (lowercased, trimmed).
  2. Each product's searchable fields (SKU, name, category) are concatenated and normalized.
  3. An exact substring match is attempted first — if found, the item scores highest.
  4. If no exact match, a word-by-word Levenshtein distance is computed between the query tokens and each product's tokens.
  5. Results are ranked by relevance score (lower distance = higher rank) and displayed in order.
  6. Items with a distance above a configurable threshold are excluded from results.

This approach handles common user errors such as: one-letter typos (refrig → refrigerator), transposed characters (smasung → Samsung), and partial words. It does not require any external search library.

11.5 Deployment — Single Standalone HTML

The application is designed for maximum deployment simplicity:

  • No server required — The HTML file can be opened directly with a browser via the file:// protocol on a local PC.
  • Static web server — For multi-device access (e.g., different POS terminals sharing the same session), serve the HTML file from any static web server (Apache, Nginx, Caddy, GitHub Pages, Netlify).
  • LAN deployment — Place the file on a PC that acts as a simple HTTP server on the local network; all branch terminals access it via IP address.
  • No database server — All data is stored in the browser's localStorage on each client device. Each device maintains its own independent data store.
  • Updates — To update the application, replace the HTML file on the server. Users refreshing the browser will receive the new version automatically.
⚠ Warning Because data is stored per-device in localStorage, each workstation has its own independent data. There is no automatic data synchronization between terminals. If a sale is made at the Iligan terminal, it will not automatically appear on the Ozamis terminal's reports. A centralized database integration (e.g., Cyrabell backend sync) is required for multi-device shared data. Contact Nexarch for cloud sync options.

12. Troubleshooting

This section addresses the most common issues encountered when using or deploying the system.

12.1 Blank Page on Load

Symptom: The application opens to a completely blank or white page. The navigation bar does not appear.

Causes and Solutions:

  • Browser too old — The application requires a browser released in 2022 or later. Update Chrome, Edge, or Firefox to the latest version. Safari 16+ is required on macOS/iOS.
  • JavaScript disabled — The application is entirely JavaScript-driven. Ensure JavaScript is enabled in browser settings.
  • CDN load failure — If the workstation has no internet access, the React and Babel CDN scripts cannot load. Check internet connectivity or switch to the offline-bundled version (contact Nexarch).
  • Corrupted localStorage — Rarely, localStorage data can become corrupted. Open browser DevTools (F12), go to Application → Local Storage, and clear all entries for the app's origin. Caution: this will erase all data and reset the app to seed data.
✓ Tip Press F12 to open browser DevTools. The Console tab shows any JavaScript errors that can help diagnose load failures. Share any red error messages with Nexarch support.

12.2 Stock Not Updating After a Sale

Symptom: A sale is completed at the POS but the inventory count for the sold items has not decreased.

Causes and Solutions:

  • Wrong warehouse selected at POS — The stock deduction occurs at the warehouse selected in the POS location selector. If the Ozamis terminal has Iligan selected, Iligan's stock will be decremented. Verify the selected warehouse and create a correcting stock adjustment (Section 3.4).
  • Transaction not fully completed — If the browser was closed or the page was refreshed before clicking "Complete Sale," the transaction may not have been saved. Check the Transaction Log in Reports to confirm whether the sale was recorded.
  • Filter applied in Inventory view — Confirm no warehouse filter is hiding the updated location's stock. Clear all filters to see combined stock.
  • localStorage not refreshed — Hard-refresh the page with Ctrl+Shift+R (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+R (macOS) to force the app to reload and re-read stored data.

12.3 Print Issues

Symptom: Printed receipts or documents are cut off, missing elements, or formatted incorrectly.

Causes and Solutions:

  • Incorrect paper size — Ensure the correct paper size is selected in your print dialog. Receipts are formatted for 80mm thermal or A4. POs and financial statements use A4.
  • Margins set too large — In the print dialog, set margins to "Minimum" or "None" for receipts, and "Default" for A4 documents.
  • Background graphics disabled — If colored headers or background shading are not printing, enable "Background graphics" / "Print backgrounds" in the browser's print settings.
  • Wrong printer selected — Ensure the correct receipt printer or office printer is selected in the print dialog dropdown.
  • Pop-up blocked — Some documents open in a new tab for printing. If nothing appears, check that your browser is not blocking pop-ups from the app's URL. Add the URL to the pop-up exceptions list.

12.4 Data Reset on Refresh

Symptom: After refreshing the browser or reopening the app, all data (products, transactions, suppliers) appears to have reset to the initial sample data.

Cause: This is the most critical issue in a localStorage-based system. It occurs when:

  • The browser's localStorage for the app's origin was cleared (manually, by browser cleanup, or by a privacy extension).
  • The user is accessing the app from a different browser or a private/incognito window.
  • The browser storage limit (~5–10MB) was exceeded and the browser automatically cleared old data.
  • The operating system or browser was updated and cleared its storage.

Prevention:

  • Regularly export data backups: navigate to Admin → Data Management → Export All Data. Save the exported JSON file to a secure location (network drive, cloud storage).
  • Disable browser automatic cache/data clearing. In Chrome, check Settings → Privacy and Security → Cookies and Site Data, and ensure the site is not set to "Clear on exit."
  • Do not use incognito/private browsing mode for operational use — storage in incognito mode is automatically deleted when the window closes.
  • Contact Nexarch about the cloud-backed Cyrabell data sync option for persistent, server-side storage.
✖ Caution There is no automatic backup. If localStorage is cleared without a manual export, all transaction history, custom product data, and accounting records will be lost permanently. Establish a daily data export routine immediately upon go-live.

13. Glossary

Key terms used throughout this manual and within the system interface.

TermDefinition
SKU Stock Keeping Unit. A unique alphanumeric code assigned to each distinct product in the inventory. In this system, SKUs follow the format CC-NNN (e.g., RF-001). SKUs are used to identify products in POS searches, purchase orders, and stock adjustments.
PO (Purchase Order) Purchase Order. A formal commercial document issued by a buyer to a supplier requesting the delivery of specific goods at agreed quantities and prices. In this system, POs progress through Draft → Open → Partial → Closed statuses.
Reorder Point The minimum stock level for a product at which a replenishment order should be placed. When on-hand stock falls to or below this level, the system flags the product as Low and includes it in reorder suggestions. Setting this correctly prevents stockouts.
Double-Entry Accounting The foundational accounting principle that every financial transaction affects at least two accounts — one is debited and one is credited — and total debits must always equal total credits. This ensures the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) always holds. All transactions in this system use double-entry.
COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) Cost of Goods Sold. The direct cost incurred to produce or purchase the goods that were sold during a period. In this system, COGS is automatically recognized at the point of sale using the weighted average cost method. It appears as an expense on the Profit & Loss statement.
AR (Accounts Receivable) Accounts Receivable. Amounts owed to Everose Marketing Corp. by customers who purchased on credit (Terms payment method). AR is an asset on the Balance Sheet. The AR Aging report tracks how long each balance has been outstanding.
AP (Accounts Payable) Accounts Payable. Amounts owed by Everose Marketing Corp. to suppliers for goods received but not yet paid for. AP is a current liability on the Balance Sheet. Each goods receipt creates an AP entry that is cleared when the supplier invoice is paid.
Trial Balance A listing of all general ledger accounts with their debit or credit balances for a given period. The total of all debit balances must equal the total of all credit balances. The Trial Balance is used to verify mathematical accuracy before preparing formal financial statements.
Weighted Average Cost The inventory costing method used by this system. Each time new stock is received, the average cost per unit is recalculated as: (Total Inventory Value + New Receipt Value) ÷ (Existing Units + Received Units). This new average is used for all future COGS recognition.
Cycle Count A method of inventory auditing where a subset of products is physically counted on a regular schedule, rather than counting all inventory at once. In this system, a Cycle Count stock adjustment is used to correct the system quantity to match the physical count.
Write-Off The removal of inventory from the books when goods are damaged, lost, stolen, or otherwise no longer available for sale. A write-off creates an accounting entry that recognizes the loss as an expense.
Levenshtein Distance A string metric used in the system's fuzzy search engine. It measures the minimum number of single-character edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions) required to change one word into another. A lower distance means a closer match.
localStorage A browser-provided storage mechanism that allows web applications to persist data on the user's device. Unlike cookies, localStorage data does not expire automatically. This system uses localStorage as its primary data store. Data is device- and browser-specific.
Journal Entry A record in the accounting system that documents a financial transaction using debits and credits across two or more accounts. Journal entries are the fundamental building blocks of the accounting ledger from which all financial reports are derived.
Gross Profit Net Sales Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold. It represents the profit earned from sales activities before deducting operating expenses (rent, salaries, utilities, etc.).
Chart of Accounts (CoA) A structured list of all financial accounts used by the organization, organized by type (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, Expenses). Each account has a unique numeric code. The CoA defines the financial reporting structure of the business.
